speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; please tell me, exactly where is the pain located and when did it start?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (likely secondary to a history of trauma and potential inflammatory etiology given family history).

Wait, before finalizing, I need to clarify the specific location of your numbness or tingling, if any, and check the results of a Tinel's test. Did you experience any clicking or popping in the wrist when you fell six months ago?

REQUEST TEST: Nerve_Conduction_Study
REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Wrist_XRay
